answer:
The mail doesn't name one league, so I can't give a single answer. It holds at least four separate Enron-linked fantasy football leagues, and only two of them show a winner.

**Eric Bass's league.** Bass signed his emails as the commissioner.
- On 2000-01-13, Eric Bass wrote to nine recipients and signed off as "The Commish".
- He wrote "The league is complete." and listed "1) The Wranglers - $281 2) Rounders - $108 3) PLOVE - $43". So The Wranglers won, based on the payouts he had collected so far.
- The email doesn't say who owned The Wranglers. This looks like the season that ended around the turn of 1999–2000.
- On 2000-06-28 he asked who wanted to play again and for suggestions on rule changes, with a draft in late August. I found no champion for his 2000 season.

**Martin Cuilla's "Big E" league.**
- On 2000-08-31, Martin Cuilla announced that the "Big E" Fantasy Football league had been set up.
- In December 2000 he was answering questions on fees, including "$125 plus $5 for free agents" and weekly prizes.
- He created a "Big E '01" league on 2001-09-06.
- Tori Kuykendall asked whether she had won anything for making the semi-finals. I found no email naming that league's champion.

**Other leagues.**
- In Eric McMurry's COLFFL, the Cartel beat the River Rats 87 to 73 in the Superbowl (2001-12-26). McMurry's address is at El Paso, so this may not be an Enron league.
- Jason Williams called himself "The Greatest DeFacto Commissioner in FFL History" and wrote up the December 2000 playoff matchups. I found no champion for his league.
- Dave Ryan set up a "Hustlers" league in September 2001, with no results in the mail.

**Not fantasy leagues.** The "Picks of the Week" emails from Eldon are a weekly pick'em pool. In that pool, Brady edged out Cameron by thirteen points in the 2000 regular season.

If you tell me which league you mean, I can search further. The Bass 2000 season and the Cuilla league results are the gaps.
